en.title: Working with the Agent
en.description: Write tasks as goals, scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria, and check tools and approvals during execution.
en.body: Working with the Agent State the goal, allowed scope, deliverables, and stop conditions clearly so that every step the Agent takes can be checked. The four parts of an executable task Part Question to answer Example --- --- --- Goal What problem should ultimately be solved? Find the root cause of the failing test Scope Where may the Agent read and modify? Only the current package; do not change public APIs Constraints Which actions must not run automatically? Do not install dependencies or access the internet Acceptance How do you prove it is done? Relevant tests pass, with the root cause and changes explained Recommended template: text Goal: ... Scope: ... Constraints: ... Deliverables: ... How it will be accepted: ... Stop if: ... Read first, plan next, write last For unfamiliar projects or research data, three rounds are recommended: 1. Read-only analysis : Have the Agent establish a baseline for the project, data, and risks. 2. Plan review : Check the files to be modified, output paths, dependencies, and verification method. 3. Execute and verify : Switch to the appropriate permissions, complete the writes, and review the diff. Shows the task text and execution status. Check input files Add material through Attach file in the input area, drag and drop, paste, or file references. Before sending, check the file names, paths, and types in the attachment tray and remove entries you do not need to send; after sending, open a preview from the file chips below the message. Workspace path references let the Agent read files on demand; they do not automatically embed the full text in the prompt. Importing external files writes to the workspace; read-only tasks should reference existing files. For details, see Workspaces and sessions. Watch the execution During execution, focus on: - The step the Agent is currently working on - The files it actually reads - Tool calls and their parameters - Commands, return codes, and output - Files written and their target paths - Approval requests waiting for your decision Before approving, check the operation's target, scope of impact, external destinations, and recovery method. To view files or diffs, open a panel from the far-right vertical toolbar; pages that support docking can be moved to the side or bottom and viewed alongside the session. In collaborative tasks, questions are answered by the designated member; action confirmations require a note and an explicit approve or reject. After submitting a decision, keep watching the execution results, and finally have a member review the delivery and the owner accept it. See Collaboration. Correct incomplete results Don't just say "be more detailed." Cite the specific gap: You listed the entry files but did not explain the call chain from startup to the main interface. Continue the read-only analysis and list the functions and source paths in call order; mark anything speculative separately. Split long tasks Break long tasks into phases that can be accepted independently, and state the inputs, outputs, and stop conditions for each. Research tasks in particular should stop when a data audit fails, rather than continuing to generate charts and reports that look complete. Next: Workbench tools.

en.title: Workbench tools
en.description: Open tools from the right-side vertical toolbar and understand docked pages, session panels, and execution permissions.
en.body: Workbench tools The current tool entry point is the workbench's far-right vertical toolbar , with panels expanding to its left. Entries appear according to installed extensions, the current session, and available capabilities; when space is tight, open More tools , or use Customize toolbar to adjust which supported entries appear and their order. Tool Best for Key checks --- --- --- Files & Preview Browsing directories, previewing text, spreadsheets, images, or scientific objects, and referencing task inputs Workspace path, file version, and the difference between a reference and actually reading the contents Terminal Running commands and checking logs and long-running task status Working directory, parameters, return codes, and write and network impact Browser Viewing local previews or research material URL, sign-in state, downloads, and external submissions Computer Use Using Codex or Claude Code to operate browsers and Electron embedded pages Run status, system permissions, and authorization for each action Change Inspector Having the Agent review this session's file changes Requires the plugin to be installed; check overall workspace state separately with git status --short Artifacts, Checkpoints & research panels Viewing phase results, evidence, and deliverables Actual installation state, input sources, versions, and unverified items When a tool cannot be opened, check the connection, plugin, and permission settings as prompted. Docking and session panels Dockable extension pages can be moved to the left, right, bottom, or main area with the position control; multiple pages on the same edge switch via tabs. Moving a page organizes your workspace; it does not change project files or execution permissions. A session's right panel has its own layout: you can resize it, switch the bound content, split it where the panel supports it, and move forward and back through panel history. Clicking the toolbar acts on the currently focused panel; not all panels allow splitting. Confirm the current session and focused object before reviewing results. Check the actual impact of tools - Verify the workspace path, especially after switching between multiple sessions or projects. - For terminal commands, check the input, output paths, network targets, and return codes. - Browser downloads, account sign-ins, and form submissions can have external effects. - Actions in Computer Use such as sending, authorizing, deleting, and paying should be authorized individually. - A panel preview is not task acceptance; explain tool results in the session and flag failures or incomplete parts. After enabling Computer Use, check the run status and the macOS system permissions. For file inputs, see Workspaces and sessions; for permissions, see Configuring a read-only sandbox and Permissions and security.

en.title: Workspaces and sessions
en.description: Organize projects and sessions in the sidebar, and check task inputs with the attachment tray and sent-file chips.
en.body: Workspaces and sessions A workspace determines where the Agent reads files, inspects Git, and runs commands; a session stores the messages, executions, and results around one goal. The same workspace can have multiple sessions. Get to know the current layout - Left sidebar : Organizes workspaces, sessions, and navigation contributed by extensions. Expand it to view collaborative projects, My Work, and the Inbox; local account, cloud status, usage summary, and Settings sit at the bottom. - Center session area : View tasks, tool calls, and answers, and enter tasks at the bottom. - Far-right vertical toolbar : Opens panels such as Files; when space is tight, find entries under "More tools." Which tools appear depends on what is installed and available. - Docked panels : Pages that support docking can be placed on the left, right, bottom, or in the main area; the session's right panel can also be split, resized, switched, and navigated forward and back where supported. The two layouts are not the same toggle. When the sidebar is collapsed, the full account summary and project tree are hidden; expand it first when you need those entries. Open a workspace 1. In the workspace location selector, choose a local workspace or a configured, available target. 2. Select the directory containing your paper, code, or data. 3. Verify the workspace path and the project name in the sidebar, then create a session. 4. Use a new session for a new goal; continue the existing session for the same goal. Illustrates the relationship between projects and sessions. Add files: choose, drag, paste, or reference Attach file in the input area opens the file picker; you can also drag supported files into the input area or paste files and images from the clipboard. Pasting ordinary text is still handled as text. PDFs, images, scientific data, and web documents are checked against type- and size-specific rules; unsupported files or failed imports show an error. Open the Files panel from the far-right toolbar to browse, preview, and reference workspace objects. You can also type @ to find workspace files; references containing spaces use the @"directory/filename" form. Before sending, the attachment tray above the input box lists the objects to send with their type, path, and known size. You can preview references that support preview or remove entries you do not need to send this time. After sending, the sent file chips below your message keep the file name and known size; click one to preview the corresponding workspace file. It is not a pending list you can keep editing. When using attachments, check in this order: 1. Before sending, check the file names, paths, and sizes in the attachment tray, and remove entries chosen by mistake or not needed. 2. After sending, use the file chips under the message to check what was sent; when you need the Agent to analyze content, explicitly ask it to read the matching file first, then explain what it found. 3. When you reference a file already in the workspace, the Agent reads it as needed. A file chip only shows the file was added to the message; do not conclude from it that the content has been read or understood. 4. Files selected or pasted from outside the workspace are imported into the workspace's session attachment directory. Removing a tray entry does not delete the file that was already imported ; to clean up, check in the Files panel and then delete. Whether an image can be used for analysis depends on the model you use and its image support; after sending, check what was read. A read-only demo can reference existing workspace files directly, to avoid extra files from importing. Shows the purpose of directory browsing and preview; the current entry point is in the far-right vertical toolbar. Manage sessions and review changes Click a session to continue its goal, use search to find history, archive sessions you are not using for now, and restore them as needed. Save important results to the workspace or a research record before deleting. Do not mix unrelated research goals in one session. After modifying files, ask the Agent to use the Change Inspector to review this session's changes, then run git status --short to inspect the entire workspace. Closing a panel or switching sessions does not undo file modifications. A clear session opening: Read the README, dependency configuration, and main entry points in the current workspace. First give the shortest path to run and test, without installing dependencies or modifying files; list anything you cannot confirm separately. Related pages: Working with the Agent, Workbench tools, Identity & Access.
